# Google Analytics MCP: Official vs Community Server
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/google-analytics-mcp-vs-official/


# Google Analytics MCP: Official vs. Community Server

Google maintains an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Google Analytics under the `googleanalytics/google-analytics-mcp` repository, while this repository (`surendranb/google-analytics-mcp`) powers `ga4mcp.com`.

Both implementations connect AI clients to Google Analytics 4, but they solve different problems. This comparison outlines their technical differences, security models, and ideal use cases.

## Architectural Overview

| Dimension | Google's Official Analytics MCP | This Server (`google-analytics-mcp`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Status & License** | Experimental · Apache-2.0 | Production · MIT |
| **Maintainer** | Google Analytics Developer Team | Surendran B (Open-Source Community) |
| **Transport Model** | Hosted Remote Endpoint (`analyticsdata.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`) | Local `stdio` Subprocess (`uvx` / `npx`) |
| **Authentication** | Google Cloud OAuth / ADC via Browser | Service Account JSON Key / 1-Click OAuth |
| **Data Privacy** | Credentials routed via Google Cloud endpoints | Local execution; zero third-party intermediaries |
| **API Coverage** | Data API + Admin API + Google Ads Links | Data API Reporting + Property Schema Discovery |
| **Schema Validation** | Direct API forwarding (API returns 400 on error) | Pre-flight validation against live property schema |
| **Total Aggregations** | Raw rows returned (model sums rows) | GA4-computed server-side totals (`metricAggregations`) |
| **Methodology Layer** | None (Model invents analysis steps) | 16 built-in analytical skills loaded on demand |
| **Setup Recovery** | Client config restart required | In-session interactive credential repair (`setup_ga4_access`) |

## Key Technical Differences

### 1. Hosted Endpoint vs. Local Stdio Execution
Google's official server is designed around a hosted remote endpoint. Your AI client connects directly to Google Cloud's MCP gateway at `https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`. This requires zero local package installation.

This community server runs as a local subprocess on your machine over standard input/output (`stdio`). It executes via `uvx google-analytics-mcp` or `npx -y @surendranb/google-analytics-mcp`. The credentials remain in your local environment, and outgoing requests travel directly to Google Analytics over standard HTTPS.

### 2. Schema Interception vs. Raw API Forwarding
The most frequent point of failure when querying GA4 with an AI model is **vocabulary drift**:
- Models often guess Universal Analytics metrics like `pageviews` instead of `screenPageViews`.
- Models guess `conversions` instead of `keyEvents`.

Google's official server forwards the model's exact request to the Data API. If the field is invalid, Google returns a 400 error. The model must guess again or fail.

This server intercepts the request before it executes. It compares requested fields against the property's live metadata via `search_schema`. If a field is invalid, it returns the correct GA4 equivalent immediately, preventing wasted tokens and failed query loops.

### 3. Server-Side Totals vs. Client-Side Model Arithmetic
When pulling multi-day or multi-page reports, ratios and averages cannot be calculated by adding up individual rows:
- Weekly bounce rate is not the average of seven daily bounce rates.
- E-commerce conversion rate is not the sum of page conversion rates.

This community server automatically injects `metricAggregations: ["TOTAL"]` into multi-row queries. It delivers the official Google-computed total alongside the raw rows, ensuring the AI model cites mathematical truth rather than guessing mental math.

### 4. Built-in Analytical Skills
Google's server provides the raw tools (`runReport`, `runRealtimeReport`). It leaves analytical methodology entirely to the language model.

This community server packages **16 analytical skills**:
- `traffic-diagnosis`: Step-by-step triage for sudden spikes or drops.
- `ai-referral-analysis`: Filter configurations for ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.
- `bot-traffic-detection`: Indicators for datacenter ASN spikes and zero-engagement sessions.
- `attribution-scope`: Rules to prevent mixing user, session, and event scopes.

When an AI agent is asked an analytical question, it calls `search_skills`, loads the verified recipe, and follows the structured framework.

## When to Use Google's Official Server
- You want a server maintained directly by Google's engineering team.
- You need deep Admin API operations, such as creating new measurement streams, managing user permissions, or linking Google Ads accounts programmatically.
- You prefer a hosted remote MCP server with no local Python or Node environment requirements.

## When to Use This Community Server
- You want production-grade natural language analytics in Claude, Cursor, VS Code, or Gemini CLI.
- You need pre-flight validation so the agent never fails on renamed or invalid dimension names.
- You need mathematically sound ratios, bounce rates, and period totals computed by GA4 server-side.
- You want local `stdio` execution where credentials stay on your machine.
- You want 16 bundled playbooks to guide the agent through traffic drops, e-commerce, and bot filtering.

## Next Steps

- **[Installation Guide](/setup/)**: Set up this community server in one line.
- **[Skills Overview](/skills/)**: Explore the 16 bundled analytical recipes.
- **[Client Setup Guides](/ga4-mcp-for-every-harness/)**: Instructions for Cursor, Claude, and 15 other AI clients.



# Fix GA4 Missing Permissions: Service Account 403 Guide
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/iam/


# Fix Google Analytics Missing Permissions (403 Error)

If you see this error, the credentials worked. The query reached Google and Google said no:

```text
IAM Error: The service account does not have Viewer access to the GA4 property
```

Nothing is wrong with your JSON key, your file path, or your property ID. The service account exists, it authenticated, and it has no permission on that property. Adding it is nine clicks.

## The nine steps

You need the `client_email` value from your service-account JSON key. It looks like `my-agent@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Open the key file in any text editor and copy that field — not `client_id`, not the private key.

1. Open [analytics.google.com](https://analytics.google.com).
2. Select the property whose ID matches your `GA4_PROPERTY_ID`.
3. Click **Admin**, the gear at the bottom left.
4. In the **Property** column, click **Property access management**.
5. Click the blue **+** at the top right, then **Add users**.
6. Paste the `client_email` into the email field.
7. Leave **Notify new users by email** switched off. It is a robot address and the mail bounces.
8. Under **Direct roles**, tick **Viewer**. Do not tick Administrator.
9. Click **Add**.

Retry the query. It works immediately — there is no propagation delay on property access.

## When Viewer is not enough

The server is read-only, so Viewer covers every tool it ships. Two situations need more:

- You are querying **real-time reports** on a property where the service account was added to an account rather than a property. Add it at the property level instead.
- You are using `list_properties` across several properties. The service account needs access to each one it should see. It returns only what it can read, and an empty list means zero properties, not a broken install.

> **Note:** these steps change a permission on a live Google property. If you are not the property owner, someone who is has to do this. There is no API path around it and no workaround that keeps Viewer off.

## Still failing after the add

Work through these in order. Each one has a distinct error message.

**`PERMISSION_DENIED` with a property ID in the message.** The property ID in your config is not the one you granted access to. Compare the two numbers digit by digit. This is common when someone has both a GA4 and an old UA property with similar names.

**`API has not been used in project ... before or it is disabled`.** The Analytics Data API is off. Enable it in the Google Cloud console under **APIs & Services → Library**.

**`invalid_grant` or `ADCExpired`.** Your `gcloud` session expired. Run `gcloud auth application-default login` again. If you use a JSON key, this error means the key was deleted or rotated.

**`The caller does not have permission` on `list_properties`.** The service account has no access at the account level. This is expected and harmless if the property-level grant above is in place.

## Let the agent check for you

If the client can reach the server at all, this returns the same decision tree offline:

```text
get_troubleshooting_guide(topic="iam")
```

Or run the interactive fix:

```text
setup_ga4_access()
```

## Next

[Setup](/setup/) for creating the service account key, [troubleshooting](/troubleshooting/) for common 400 and quota errors, and [query shapes](/schema/) for filter syntax.

<section class="section">
<h2 class="section__h">An agent with a GA4 tool guesses. That is the whole problem.</h2>
<p class="section__sub">Three failures show up every time someone points a general-purpose model at the Analytics Data API.</p>
<div class="grid3">
<div class="feat"><h3>It invents field names</h3><p>Models are trained on Universal Analytics vocabulary. <code>pageviews</code> instead of <code>screenPageViews</code>. The API returns a 400 and the agent retries with another guess.</p></div>

</div>
</section>

<section class="section">
<h2 class="section__h">What this server does about it</h2>
<p class="section__sub">Three mechanisms, all of them inside the tool call. Nothing here depends on the model behaving well.</p>
<div class="grid3">
<div class="feat"><h3>Schema check before the query</h3><p><code>get_ga4_data</code> validates every dimension and metric name against your live property. A wrong name comes back with the reason and the correct spelling, not a 400 and a retry loop.</p></div>
<div class="feat"><h3>Skills loaded on demand</h3><p>Sixteen recipes ship in the package — traffic diagnosis, ecommerce, attribution scope, AI referral split. The agent loads one before it analyzes, so the method is fixed instead of improvised.</p></div>
<div class="feat"><h3>Totals computed by GA4</h3><p>Every multi-row pull returns a <code>totals</code> block that GA4 computed server-side. The model reads the period figure instead of adding up rows and drifting.</p></div>
</div>
</section>

<section class="section">
<h2 class="section__h">What it does when the setup is broken</h2>
<p class="section__sub">Most failures are not analysis failures. They are a missing property ID, an expired token, or a service account that was never added to the property. The server handles all three inside the session.</p>
<div class="grid3">
<div class="feat"><h3>Setup recovery mid-session</h3><p><code>setup_ga4_access</code> collects the missing value and reconnects without a restart. No client config editing, no reinstall.</p></div>
<div class="feat"><h3>Guides bundled offline</h3><p><code>get_troubleshooting_guide</code> serves the setup, IAM and schema fix paths from inside the package. It works with no network and no API access.</p></div>
<div class="feat"><h3>Row guard before the pull</h3><p>Large queries are estimated first and warn above 2,500 rows, so one careless question does not fill the context window with raw rows.</p></div>
</div>
</section>

<section class="section">
<h2 class="section__h">Against Google's own server</h2>
<p class="section__sub">Google ships an official Analytics MCP server, and it is genuinely good. Here is the honest split.</p>
<div class="compare">
<div>
<h4>Google's Analytics MCP</h4>
<ul>
<li>Admin API plus Data API: accounts, properties, Google Ads links, core and funnel reports, realtime.</li>
<li>Hosted remote endpoint at <code>analyticsdata.googleapis.com/mcp/v1</code> — no local install at all.</li>
<li>Apache-2.0, labelled Experimental, maintained by the Analytics organisation.</li>
<li>Best choice when you want zero install and a vendor-maintained toolset.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div>
<h4>This server</h4>
<ul>
<li>Reporting and metadata, with the analysis layer attached: 16 skills, schema validation, GA4-computed totals, row guard.</li>
<li>Local stdio over your own credentials. Nothing leaves your machine except GA4 API calls.</li>
<li>MIT, one maintainer, and a fix path for the three errors that actually stop people.</li>
<li>Best choice when the agent has to reason about the numbers, not just fetch them.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<p style="margin-top:1.2rem;font-size:.95rem"><a href="/google-analytics-mcp-vs-official/">Read the full technical comparison: Community stdio vs Google Hosted MCP →</a></p>
</section>

# Natural Language Google Analytics: Query GA4 with AI
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/natural-language-google-analytics/


# Natural Language Google Analytics

Querying Google Analytics 4 through a conversation changes how teams extract marketing insights. Instead of building custom explorations in the GA4 web UI, writing BigQuery SQL, or navigating the Analytics Data API documentation, you ask questions in plain English and receive structured, verified answers.

General-purpose language models fail when pointed directly at the Google Analytics Data API without a specialized protocol layer. This guide explains why naive LLM queries fail, how the Model Context Protocol (MCP) fixes them, and how to query your analytics with natural language.

## Why General LLMs Fail on Google Analytics 4

Every developer who asks an untuned AI to query GA4 encounters three structural failures:

### 1. Universal Analytics Vocabulary Hallucination
Language models were trained on millions of pages of Universal Analytics (UA) documentation and StackOverflow answers written prior to July 2023. When asked for traffic data, models reflexively generate queries containing `ga:sessions`, `pageviews`, `uniquePageviews`, and `bounces`.

In the GA4 Data API:
- `pageviews` does not exist; the dimension is `pagePath` and the metric is `screenPageViews`.
- `conversions` was renamed to `keyEvents` on May 6, 2024.
- `ga:` prefixes cause hard 400 validation errors.

An unassisted model enters a retry loop, guessing variations until hitting API rate limits.

### 2. Incompatible Dimensional Scopes
GA4 enforces strict separation between user-scoped, session-scoped, and event-scoped data:
- `firstUserDefaultChannelGroup` (user-scoped) cannot be paired with event-scoped metrics like `eventCount` without distorting attribution.
- Session dimensions require session metrics.

When an AI guesses dimension pairings, the GA4 API rejects the request with: `The request's dimensions and metrics are incompatible.`

### 3. Mental Arithmetic Drift on Ratios and Averages
If an agent pulls seven daily rows and calculates the weekly bounce rate, average session duration, or conversion rate, it sums or averages the ratio column. Ratios and averages do not sum arithmetically. The resulting figures look plausible but are mathematically incorrect.

## How GA4 MCP Solves Natural Language Queries

The GA4 MCP server acts as an intelligent intermediary between your AI harness (Claude, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI) and the Google Analytics Data API.

```
┌─────────────────┐       Natural Language Question       ┌────────────────────────┐
│  Claude / Cursor│ ────────────────────────────────────► │  GA4 MCP Coordinator   │
└─────────────────┘                                       └───────────┬────────────┘
         ▲                                                            │
         │ Verified Response + Totals                                 ▼
┌────────┴────────┐       Validated API Request           ┌────────────────────────┐
│  GA4 Data API   │ ◄──────────────────────────────────── │ Pre-Flight Validation  │
│  (Google Cloud) │                                       │ • Property Schema Match│
└─────────────────┘                                       │ • Scope Compatibility  │
                                                          │ • Server-Side Totals   │
                                                          └────────────────────────┘
```

Three mechanisms guarantee accuracy:

1. **Pre-Flight Schema Validation**: Before executing any request, `get_ga4_data` inspects the live metadata of your property. If an agent requests an invalid field, the server intercepts the call and returns the valid GA4 equivalent.
2. **Deterministic Skills on Demand**: When an agent faces an analytical task, it loads a local skill (`traffic-diagnosis`, `ecommerce-analysis`, `attribution-scope`). The skill dictates the proven dimensions, metrics, and interpretation rules.
3. **GA4 Server-Side Totals**: The server requests `metricAggregations: ["TOTAL"]` directly from Google. The agent reports the Google-computed total rather than performing client-side math.

## Ten Natural Language Questions You Can Ask Today

Once configured in your AI client, you can ask questions directly in your editor or chat terminal:

### Traffic & Acquisition
- *"What were our top 5 acquisition channels by sessions over the last 30 days, and which had the highest engagement rate?"*
- *"Compare this week's active users with last week's. Did organic search or direct traffic drive the variance?"*
- *"Show me all referral traffic from AI platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) for the past 90 days."*

### Content & Engagement
- *"Which blog posts had the highest average engagement time among users from organic search this month?"*
- *"List the top 10 landing pages with the highest bounce rate that received at least 200 sessions."*
- *"What are our top pages viewed by mobile users compared to desktop users?"*

### E-Commerce & Conversions
- *"What is our overall checkout-to-purchase conversion rate across the last 60 days?"*
- *"Which traffic channel produced the highest average order value (AOV) last month?"*
- *"Show me purchase revenue broken down by country and city for the last quarter."*

### Technical & Anomaly Detection
- *"Did our site experience an abnormal spike in direct traffic yesterday? Check city and device category to verify if it was bot traffic."*

## Local Stdio Architecture & Data Privacy

Security is a primary concern when connecting analytics to AI assistants. Cloud-hosted analytics SaaS wrappers require passing your Google Cloud credentials to third-party servers.

GA4 MCP operates entirely over local **stdio transport**:
- **Direct Connection**: All communication travels over stdin/stdout between your local AI harness and the local Python subprocess.
- **No Third-Party Relay**: API calls travel directly from your machine to `https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com` via your own Google Cloud Service Account.
- **Zero Query Retention**: Your analytics numbers never touch external proxy databases or third-party loggers.

- **[Installation Guide](/setup/)**: Step-by-step setup using the 1-line auto-installer or native package managers.
- **[Prompt Cookbook](/google-analytics-ai-prompts/)**: 35 production-tested prompts across e-commerce, SEO, and acquisition.
- **[Client Configuration](/ga4-mcp-for-every-harness/)**: How to add GA4 MCP to Cursor, Claude, VS Code, and 14 other environments.



# GA4 MCP plugins for Claude Code and Gemini CLI
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/ga4-plugins/


# Plugins

A plugin is a manifest that tells a client how to launch the server and what values it needs. It is not a different server. It is the same `uvx google-analytics-mcp` with the configuration attached, so the client can install and prompt for the two values in one flow instead of asking you to edit a JSON file.

Two clients support a plugin bundle today.

<!--PLUGINS-->

## When a plugin is worth it

If you install the server once, on one machine, the plain config entry is simpler and this page adds nothing. A plugin pays off when you want the client to ask for `GA4_PROPERTY_ID` and the credentials path itself, or when you are distributing the setup to other people and do not want them editing config files.

## What is inside

Both bundles carry the same two declarations:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "command": "uvx",
    "args": ["google-analytics-mcp"]
  },
  "settings": [
    { "name": "GA4_PROPERTY_ID", "required": true, "type": "string" },
    { "name": "GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS", "required": true, "type": "string" }
  ]
}
```

The `settings` array is what makes the client prompt. The `mcp` block is what it launches. Everything else is metadata — name, version, license, repository.

## Next

If you would rather not use a bundle, the per-client guides show the raw config: [Claude](/ga4-mcp-for-claude/), [Gemini CLI](/ga4-mcp-for-gemini/), or the [full client list](/ga4-mcp-for-every-harness/).



# Privacy — what the GA4 MCP server sends
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/privacy/


# Privacy

Short version: the server runs on your machine, talks to Google with your credentials, never writes to your property, and sends anonymous usage counts that you can turn off with one variable.

## What stays local

Your credentials, your service-account key, your property ID, and every report the server returns. Queries go from your machine to `analyticsdata.googleapis.com` and the rows come back to your machine. Nothing passes through studio infrastructure.

## What is sent

The server posts anonymous usage events to `ga4.builditwithai.xyz`, a Cloudflare Worker that forwards them to the studio's analytics. One event per lifecycle step, not per query.

Each event carries:

- a random installation identifier, generated on first run. It is not derived from your machine, your Google account, or your credentials
- the event name — for example `mcp_started`, `tool_executed`, `server_first_install`
- the tool name that ran, and whether it succeeded
- an error category on failure, such as `InitError` or `IAMError`
- duration in milliseconds
- the client name and version the server was launched by
- the server version

## What is not sent

- your credentials, tokens, or key file path
- your GA4 property ID — numeric IDs are redacted to `<id>` before sending
- report rows, metrics, dimensions, or anything the GA4 API returned
- file paths, email addresses, or hostnames

One caveat worth stating: `get_ga4_data` accepts an optional `intent` string that describes the question in plain English. That string is recorded with the tool event so the studio can tell which questions the server answers badly. If your intent text contains something you would not send, omit it. The field is optional and the tool works without it.

## Turning it off

Any one of these does it:

```bash
export DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1
```

```bash
export DO_NOT_TRACK=1
```

```bash
export NO_TELEMETRY=1
```

The check happens before any network call, so with one of them set the server makes no request to studio infrastructure at all. It still works exactly the same.

## Third parties

The site at ga4mcp.com uses Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, and Plausible to count page views. The MCP server itself does not load any of them, and none is involved in a query.

## Contact

Open an issue at [github.com/surendranb/google-analytics-mcp](https://github.com/surendranb/google-analytics-mcp) for any question about this page.



# GA4 query shapes — filters, field names and totals
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/schema/


# Query shapes

`get_ga4_data` takes filters in the shape of the Google Analytics Data API v1beta schema. It is not SQL, and it is not a query string. This page is the six shapes that cover every filter you will write, copied exactly.

## The rule that prevents most errors

**One top-level key per expression.** A filter expression has exactly one of these keys, and nothing else beside it:

- `filter` — a single condition
- `andGroup` — all conditions must match
- `orGroup` — any condition may match
- `notExpression` — invert one condition

Two keys in the same object is the most common 400. The server translates between `camelCase` and `snake_case`, so `fieldName` and `field_name` both work, but the structure still has to be right.

## Exact match on a string

Cities that are exactly London:

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "fieldName": "city",
    "stringFilter": {
      "matchType": "EXACT",
      "value": "London"
    }
  }
}
```

`matchType` accepts `EXACT`, `BEGINS_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `CONTAINS`, `FULL_REGEXP` and `PARTIAL_REGEXP`. Regex values are case-sensitive by default; add `"caseSensitive": false` to the `stringFilter` object to relax it.

## A value from a list

Any of three countries, in one condition rather than three:

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "fieldName": "country",
    "inListFilter": {
      "values": ["United States", "United Kingdom", "Canada"]
    }
  }
}
```

`inListFilter` is the one to reach for when the model would otherwise write an `orGroup` of exact matches. It is shorter, and it cannot be malformed by nesting.

## A numeric threshold

Metrics only. Users above 100, in `metric_filter`:

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "fieldName": "activeUsers",
    "numericFilter": {
      "operation": "GREATER_THAN",
      "value": {
        "int64Value": "100"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Operations are `EQUAL`, `LESS_THAN`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL`, `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL` and `BETWEEN`. For `BETWEEN`, the value object holds `fromValue` and `toValue` instead of a single `int64Value`.

## All conditions must hold

London, on mobile:

```json
{
  "andGroup": {
    "expressions": [
      {
        "filter": {
          "fieldName": "city",
          "stringFilter": {
            "matchType": "EXACT",
            "value": "London"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "filter": {
          "fieldName": "deviceCategory",
          "stringFilter": {
            "matchType": "EXACT",
            "value": "Mobile"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The `expressions` array is required and the key is `andGroup`, not `and`. Writing `"and": [...]` is invalid.

## Excluding one condition

Everything except direct traffic:

```json
{
  "notExpression": {
    "filter": {
      "fieldName": "sessionDefaultChannelGroup",
      "stringFilter": {
        "matchType": "EXACT",
        "value": "Direct"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`notExpression` wraps exactly one expression. To exclude two things, use `notExpression` around an `orGroup`.

## Field names come from your property, not from training

If you get an invalid dimension or metric error, the name you used does not exist in that property. It is usually a Universal Analytics name — `pageviews`, `users`, `conversions` — and GA4 renamed all three.

Use the search tool before typing a name:

```text
search_schema(keyword="conversions")
```

That returns `keyEvents` today, not `conversions`, because GA4 renamed the concept in 2024. The server validates field names against the live property before the query runs, so a wrong name comes back with the reason and a candidate instead of a bare 400.

For a whole category at once, `list_dimension_categories` and `list_metric_categories` return counts first; then `get_dimensions_by_category` gives you the names.

## Rows, totals and the reason both exist

Every multi-row pull returns a `totals` block that GA4 computed server-side, alongside the rows. Read the period figure from `totals`. Do not add up daily rows in the model — rates do not sum, and a seven-day total built by arithmetic is wrong while looking reasonable.

Large queries are estimated before they run and warn above 2,500 rows. If you need more than that, narrow the date range or the dimensions rather than forcing it through; a wide pull with no aggregation fills the context window and answers nothing.

## Next

If the query runs but the answer is nonsense, the problem is method rather than syntax. Read the [skills index](/skills/) and pick the recipe that matches the question.



# Install GA4 MCP: Connect Google Analytics to AI Clients
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/setup/


# Install GA4 MCP

This guide takes you from nothing to a working GA4 query inside your agent. It assumes you have a Google Analytics 4 property and an AI client that speaks MCP.

## What you need first

Three things, and only the first one is easy to get wrong.

**A GA4 property ID.** It is a number like `123456789`. You find it in Analytics under **Admin → Property details**. It is not the `G-XXXXXXXXXX` measurement ID, and it is not the numeric stream ID. Pasting the measurement ID is the single most common setup failure.

**A Google Cloud project** with the Analytics Data API enabled.

**Credentials,** picked in the next section. Either a service-account JSON key or the local `gcloud` login works.

## Step 1 — Install the server

Three routes. Pick one.

The installer is the one that also writes your client entry:

```bash
curl -fsSL "https://ga4.builditwithai.xyz/install" | bash
```

It detects your client, checks for `uv`, installs the package, and writes the MCP server entry. It covers Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code with Cline or Roo Code, Continue.dev, OpenCode, Windsurf, Zed and Google Antigravity.

If you would rather not run a script, use a runtime directly:

```bash
uvx google-analytics-mcp
```

```bash
npx -y @surendranb/google-analytics-mcp
```

Both are the same server. `uvx` is faster to start after the first run; `npx` needs Node already installed.

> **Note:** the installer writes the entry, not the credentials. You still set the two values in Step 2.

## Step 2 — Connect it to your property

The server reads two environment variables. Both belong inside the client's server entry, not in your shell profile, unless you launch the client from a shell that has them.

```bash
export GA4_PROPERTY_ID="123456789"
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/absolute/path/to/service-account.json"
```

The credentials path must be absolute. A relative path resolves against whatever directory the client happens to start in, which is not the one you expect.

**If you use a service account,** create it in the Google Cloud console under **IAM & Admin → Service Accounts**, then **Keys → Add key → JSON**. That key file is what the path points at. The service account also has to be added to the GA4 property itself — that is a separate step and it is where most people stop. The [permissions guide](/iam/) walks through it.

**If you use `gcloud` instead,** run this once and skip the key file entirely:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default login
```

Then omit `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. The server picks up application default credentials.

> **Tip:** the property ID is numeric and has no prefix. If yours starts with `G-`, you have the measurement ID, and every query will fail with a permissions error that has nothing to do with permissions.

## Step 3 — Verify it actually works

Open your client and ask this exact question:

```text
List my GA4 properties.
```

You have succeeded when the agent calls `list_properties` and returns rows. A setup error at this point is one of four things, and the next section names all of them.

Then ask one question that exercises the analysis layer:

```text
Why did organic sessions drop in the last 7 days?
```

A working install loads the `traffic-diagnosis` skill, calls `get_ga4_data`, and answers with a `totals` block rather than a summary of daily rows.

## When it fails

| What you see | What it means | Where to go |
|---|---|---|
| `InitError` on startup | One or both environment variables are missing or outside the server's `env` block | [Setup errors](/setup/#when-it-fails) |
| `IAMError` or `403` | The service account is valid but was never added to the property | [Permissions guide](/iam/) |
| `ADCExpired` or `503` | The `gcloud` login expired | Run `gcloud auth application-default login` again |
| `400` invalid dimension or metric | The field name is a UA name or a guess | [Query shapes](/schema/) and `search_schema` |

The server also carries these fix paths inside the package, so an agent can resolve most of them without a browser:

```text
get_troubleshooting_guide(topic="setup" | "iam" | "schema")
```

## Or let the agent fix it

If the client supports prompts, `setup_ga4_access` collects the missing value and reconnects without a restart. That is usually faster than editing config by hand.

## Next

Read [your client's guide](/ga4-mcp-for-every-harness/) for the exact config shape it expects, since four of the eleven clients use a different key than the rest. Then read the [skills index](/skills/) to see what the agent can do once it is connected, or browse [prompts](/google-analytics-ai-prompts/) for 35 tested templates.



# GA4 skills — sixteen analytical recipes for your agent
URL: https://ga4mcp.com/skills/


# Skills

A skill is a short playbook that ships inside the package. The agent calls `search_skills` with a keyword, gets one back as markdown, and follows it. Nothing is fetched over the network, so it works with no API access and no credentials.

The point is to replace improvisation. Ask a general model why traffic dropped and it will invent a method. Ask it to run `traffic-diagnosis` and it runs the same six checks every time, in the same order, because the method is data instead of a guess.

## How the agent uses them

```text
search_skills("drop")
```

```text
search_skills("traffic-diagnosis")
```

An empty query returns the index. The full text of a skill arrives as markdown, and the agent uses the dimensions and metrics named inside it rather than choosing its own.

## When to load one

Before any question that involves interpretation, not just retrieval. "How many sessions yesterday" needs no skill. "Why did sessions drop", "which channel is worth more", "is this bot traffic" all do.

<!--SKILLS-->

## Next

[Query shapes](/schema/) covers the filter syntax these skills assume. If a skill names a metric your property does not have, `search_schema` will tell you what that property calls it.
